key_insight: This image-based surgical site infection AI model showed similar performance across age, gender, race, and skin color, but performance varied by geography.
clinical_relevance: The study highlights why fairness testing is needed before deploying clinical AI, so performance gaps across sites or regions do not create unequal care.
method: Retrospective multicenter model development and validation using postoperative incision images submitted through the electronic health record.
Compared AUROC across age, gender, geography, race, and skin color subgroups.
Used both internal training data and temporal validation data from later years.
evidence_signal: Training included 13,702 images from 4,274 patients, and temporal validation included 4,242 images from 1,353 patients; subgroup AUROC differences were minimal except for geography.
watch_item: The dataset was heavily concentrated in White/light-skin patients and certain regions, so broader external validation is still needed before widespread use.
paper_title: Assessment of Fairness and Bias of an Image-based Surgical Site Infection Detection AI Model
